title: Appeals and Grievances Filing Deadline — Counting Rules and Late Filings
content:
### Appeals and Grievances: the filing deadline and how it is counted

**Rule 1 — where the date comes from.** The initial determination date is taken from the subject record — the posted date of the claim line (the Explanation of Benefits date), the decision date of the authorization denial, or the disenrollment or termination date of the enrollment — never from the caller.

**Rule 2 — retired clause.** "The case must be received no later than the tier's filing deadline after the initial determination recorded on the subject record." This clause is **no longer in force**; the current basis governs in its place.

**Rule 3 — counting.** The deadline is counted in calendar days starting the day after the initial determination date, so the last timely day is that date plus the tier's filing deadline in days, and a case received on that day is timely while one received the next day is late.

**Rule 4 — which date of the filing counts.** Timeliness is measured under the tier's "deadline measured by" entry, which on every tier is the date the region receives the filing.

**Rule 5 — late cases.** A late case is dismissed as untimely unless late filing with good cause is accepted on the tier and a statement of good cause documenting one of the tier's good cause examples is on file, in which case it proceeds as if timely.

**Counting worked through (hypothetical dates).** An initial determination recorded on 2026-03-02, on a tier with a 90-day filing deadline: day 1 of the count is 2026-03-03; the last timely day is 2026-05-31.

| Date the region receives the case | Result |
|---|---|
| 2026-05-30 | timely |
| 2026-05-31 (the last timely day) | timely |
| 2026-06-01 (the next day) | late |

**Late cases — branch table**

| Late filing with good cause accepted on the tier | Statement of good cause documenting a listed example on file | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | proceeds as if timely |
| yes | no | dismissed as untimely |
| no | yes or no | dismissed as untimely |

The dates are those on the system records: the determination date from the subject record, and the receipt date of the filing.

superseded_clauses: The case must be received no later than filing_deadline_days after the initial determination recorded on the subject record.
